messages.content: You are BioGPT, an expert compiler architect. Translate the provided natural language biological protocol into valid, deterministic BioScript code for execution on a microfluidic biochip.

Source link: https://microfluidics.utoronto.ca/papers/ARAC%20review.pdf
Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-anchem-062011-143028

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidics (DMF) Oil-Free Homogeneous Enzyme Kinetics Assay — Alkaline Phosphatase (AP) Activity and Inorganic-Phosphate Product Inhibition, Monitored via Fluorescein Diphosphate (FDP) Fluorogenic Substrate

REAGENTS USED:
  - Alkaline Phosphatase (AP) enzyme droplets
  - Fluorescein Diphosphate (FDP) fluorogenic substrate droplets
  - Inorganic Phosphate solution (product-inhibition titrant)
  - Distilled Water (dilution/quench droplets)

STEPS:
1. Dispense an AP droplet and an FDP droplet on an oil-free DMF device.
2. Merge and actively mix the AP and FDP droplets to initiate the enzymatic reaction, converting FDP into fluorescent fluorescein.
3. Incubate the merged droplet at room temperature to allow the reaction to proceed.
4. Measure the baseline fluorescence intensity of the fluorescein product to establish uninhibited AP reaction kinetics.
5. Titrate inorganic phosphate into the reaction droplet across a series of points to assess product inhibition: for each point, dispense a fresh phosphate droplet, merge/mix it with the reaction droplet, incubate, and re-measure fluorescence intensity.
6. Repeat the phosphate titration/measurement cycle across multiple points to build a dose-response inhibition curve.
7. Dilute/quench the final reaction droplet with distilled water and discard it.

INTERPRETATION: Successful assay performance is confirmed by AP enzyme kinetic constants (e.g., Km, Vmax) that are consistent with values reported in the literature for conventional macroscale assays, and by a phosphate-concentration-dependent decrease in fluorescence signal consistent with competitive product inhibition — demonstrating that an oil-free DMF platform supports quantitative homogeneous enzyme kinetics studies without partitioning of hydrophobic reagents into a carrier-oil phase.

module fluorescence

manifest alkaline_phosphatase
manifest fluorescein_diphosphate
manifest inorganic_phosphate
manifest distilled_water

instructions:

ap = dispense 10 units of alkaline_phosphatase
fdp = dispense 10 units of fluorescein_diphosphate

rxn = mix ap with fdp for 30s
heat rxn at 25c for 5m

baseline_reading = detect fluorescence on rxn for 30s

repeat 4 times {
    phosphate = dispense 5 units of inorganic_phosphate
    rxn = mix rxn with phosphate for 20s
    heat rxn at 25c for 5m
    inhibition_reading = detect fluorescence on rxn for 30s
}

water = dispense 20 units of distilled_water
rxn = mix rxn with water for 15s
dispose rxn

bsbbr_2_h:
	PHI REPEAT_41 = {REPEAT_40,REPEAT_42}
	PHI inhibition_reading1 = {inhibition_reading0,inhibition_reading2}
	PHI phosphate1 = {phosphate0,phosphate2}
	PHI rxn2 = {rxn1,rxn3}
	if REPEAT_41[0] > 0	|	true: jump bsbbr_3_t	|	false: jump bsbbr_4_f
bsbbr_3_t:
	phosphate2[0] = dispense(inorganic_phosphate)
	rxn3[0] = mix(rxn2[0], phosphate2[0]) @ 20.0SECOND
	heat(rxn3[0]) @ 25.0CELSIUS @ 300.0SECOND
	inhibition_reading2[0] = detect(fluorescence, rxn3[0]) @ 30.0SECOND
	REPEAT_42[0] = REPEAT_41[0] - 1
bsbbr_4_f:
	water1[0] = dispense(distilled_water)
	rxn4[0] = mix(rxn2[0], water1[0]) @ 15.0SECOND
	dispose(rxn4[0])
	NOP

numeric_mismatches.note: The review does not report exact microliter volumes for this assay; values are authored approximations, not taken from the source text.

The review states inhibition by inorganic phosphate was studied but does not specify how many titration points were used; 4 iterations were chosen to represent a generic dose-response series.
